Market Intelligence Briefing
subheadings: 🇺🇸 United States  Mixed  hold / data dependent
🇪🇺 European Union  Bearish  stalled growth / defensive
🇨🇳 China  Bearish  weak credit / policy patience
🇯🇵 Japan  Mixed  tightening bias / fiscal drag
🇦🇺 Australia  Mixed  post-hike / no set path
🇵🇱 Poland  Mixed  growth strong / rates on hold
🧮 Earnings Pattern — What the Market Pays For
Beats are not enough: guidance and AI demand set the reaction
🔍 Underowned Themes — Active on X, Underweight in Portfolios
Copper processing margins, not the copper price
Data-centre power: the utility spending wave
Polish defence supply chain beyond the headline names
The euro as a reserve currency, not just a trade
Bitcoin is down 24% in 20 sessions, and the equity proxies fell harder
Liquidity framework: balance sheets, the dollar and credit
🔮 Anticipatory Positioning — Markets Pricing In Future Events
US-Iran talks: a deal would take the oil premium out
Bank of England: a March cut is in the price
Nvidia on Feb. 25: the guide, not the beat
The Fed under Warsh: cuts depend on inflation
$NVDA  the Feb. 25 print as a guide test  ↑
Reddit / RDDT  "sentiment crashed, revenue did not"
Nebius / NBIS  "the bulls and bears after earnings"
body: Wednesday, February 18 2026 — Macro · Sectors · Flows · Crypto

Macro Stance: Mixed. The January data are soft enough to keep cuts alive but not soft enough to end the debate: payrolls rose by 130,000 and headline inflation slowed to 2.4% over the prior year, yet core CPI picked up at the start of the year on firmer services costs. Fed speakers split on the path. Goolsbee sees several cuts this year if inflation moves back toward 2%, while Barr wants proof that goods inflation is retreating before any further cut. Equities are the weak spot: the S&P 500 is down 1.39% over 20 sessions and the VIX stands at 20.29 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17), with AI-disruption fears still driving the tape.

Rates & Curve: The US Treasury par curve at the prior close (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-17) has the 2Y at 3.43% and the 10Y at 4.05%, a 10Y−2Y spread of 62 bps. Over 20 observations the 2Y is down 16 bps and the 10Y down 19 bps, so the spread has narrowed by 3 bps: moderately steep, approaching the long-run average, and bull flattening (both down, 10Y down more). Over five observations the 10Y has fallen 17 bps. The move is a rotation into bonds rather than a new policy signal: yields hit 2026 lows as investors rotated into bonds, and the 10-year was little changed while investors waited for delayed data. The dollar index sits at 97.16, down 2.24% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17), and a BofA survey shows investors expect the 'Warsh trade' to weaken the dollar.

New / Most Important: The most important item for the rate path is the balance sheet. Warsh may want a smaller Fed balance sheet, but that is hard to achieve. Fed officials are also debating whether AI productivity lifts the neutral rate, and Barr argues the AI boom is not a reason to cut. On bank supervision the Fed is set to loosen rules to boost mortgage lending, a supportive backdrop for lenders and for housing turnover.

Playbook ✓: Stance Mixed. Own duration only in measured size. The 7-10 year Treasury ETF (IEF, up 1.32% over 20 sessions) and the 20-year ETF (TLT, up 2.36%) benefit directly if soft payroll and inflation prints keep the 10Y drifting lower, but the curve move is a bull flattening, so the 2Y-10Y spread is not a trade on its own. Hedge equity beta with VIX exposure while the S&P 500 is 1.39% lower over 20 sessions. The call turns Bearish on duration if the core inflation pickup is confirmed by the next inflation release, or if a Fed speaker takes the cut off the table, as Barr's hold comment already points toward. Size the duration position modestly until the next Fed speaker sets the bar for the first cut.

Macro Stance: Bearish on growth. Euro-area output barely expanded: the EU economy grew 0.3% in the fourth quarter, and the German chamber of commerce sees the German economy stuck at just 1% growth in 2026. Equities have done better than the data suggest. The STOXX Europe 600 closed at 621.29, up 3.07% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17), helped by financial stocks, while Europe's earnings gains are capped by lofty valuations. The rally is a valuation and sector-mix story, not a domestic demand story. The read is stalled growth rather than contraction, which argues for patience on the euro rather than a directional bet.

Activity & Inflation: Headline German inflation was soft in January: the harmonised index fell 0.1% month on month, in line with forecasts. Softer prices do not fix the growth problem the chamber describes. The Euro Stoxx 50 closed at 6,021.85, up 2.2% over 20 sessions, and the DAX at 24,998.40 is up 1.2% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17). The euro-area growth read is thin, so the market is leaning on the index's financial and defensive mix rather than on a cyclical upturn.

New / Most Important: The ECB made its euro backstop global to bolster the currency's role and revamped its euro liquidity offer to boost the currency's appeal. That is a structural euro-liquidity story, not a rate decision. Lagarde is reported to be leaving before the end of her term, and EU governments may want to fast-track the succession. Lagarde has also pushed back against taxes meant to stop capital outflows, which is the same argument the backstop makes.

Playbook ✓: Stance Bearish on European cyclicals and domestic demand, with the index support coming from financials and defensives. Keep euro exposure as a reserve-currency position rather than a growth trade: EUR/USD at 1.1850 is up 1.81% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17), and the liquidity offer is the reason to hold it. The call turns Mixed if a euro-area print beats the 1% growth read or if the ECB succession names a candidate with a clear policy line. Own large-cap defensive Europe in preference to broad cyclicals until then.

Macro Stance: Bearish on domestic demand, with a firmer currency doing some of the work. Credit is still weak: January new loans jumped but missed forecasts as weak demand persisted, and 2025 new bank loans were the lowest in seven years. The People's Bank has pledged to keep policy moderately loose, but the feed carries no new stimulus package. The export engine is losing steam too: the nation's biggest port reports a 'dismal' export picture and a freight slump.

PMIs & Activity: The latest official manufacturing PMI in the feed is January, at 49.3, a contraction reading. A private survey showed factory activity expanding faster in January, and the RatingDog services PMI beat strongly as domestic demand offset softer exports. Consumer prices rose 0.2% in January, and the statistics office has unveiled a new CPI basket composition. Japanese shipments to China soared in January, a sign that some Chinese import demand is intact.

Credit Impulse: The impulse is the weak spot. January loans rose but missed forecasts, and the feed's 2025 total is the lowest in seven years. The People's Bank added Zheshang Bank to its list of systemically important lenders, a supervision step rather than a credit-easing one, and another large bank has been put under stricter watch. Weak loan demand, not a lack of lending capacity, is the constraint the headlines describe.

Property: Home prices are still falling. New home prices extended their decline, and the South China Morning Post's read is that there is 'no floor yet' despite policy support. Caixin reports the slump eased after the stimulus push, and used-home prices fell at a slower pace. State firms are buying foreclosed properties to slow the downturn, and Vanke is downsizing its serviced-apartment business after record red ink. A green-shoots reading is still shaky.

Fiscal, Policy & Trade: Provinces are cutting revenue outlooks, and analysts warn about debt control. Beijing is opening access selectively: zero-tariff access for 53 African nations from May, and a pause on tech bans ahead of a Xi summit. China confirmed talks about a Trump visit while the trade truce stays on the cards. The state is tightening its hold on rare-earth metals, and the premier toured the rare-earths production hub. Xi's agenda puts domestic demand and tech independence first.

Markets & Flows: The Hang Seng closed at 26,705.94, up 0.53% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-16), while the Shanghai Composite at 4,082.07 is down 0.48% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13). The China large-cap ETF FXI at 38.52 is down 1.98% and the internet ETF KWEB at 32.72 is down 8.37% over 20 sessions; ASHR, the CSI 300 tracker, is up 0.89% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17). The yuan is firmer: USD/CNY at 6.9080 is down 0.86% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17). Hong Kong closed the lunar year with its best performance in eight years, but Beijing's 'national team' of investors is working to keep the AI stock boom in check. The firmer yuan also gives the People's Bank room to focus on domestic demand.

New / Most Important: The yuan is the story. China let the yuan rise to its strongest level in years as the de-dollarisation trend grows, and FX conversion eased from a record as the appreciation slowed. Economists are urging looser capital controls as the dollar dips, and Xi touts the 'super-large' domestic market as the key to boosting local demand. MSCI tilted its index revamp toward Chinese tech, which gives foreign flows a reason to return to the mainland tech names.

Playbook ✓: Stance Bearish. Do not chase the Hong Kong or Shanghai rebound on the yuan story alone. Prefer hedged yuan exposure through the currency, and stay underweight credit-sensitive internet names (KWEB, down 8.37% over 20 sessions) until new loans and property prices stabilise together. The call turns Mixed on a loan print that beats forecasts with household borrowing rising, plus a turn in the home-price series. ⚠ Divergence: the yuan is at its strongest in years and Hong Kong has just closed its best lunar-year run in eight years, while January new loans missed forecasts.

Macro Stance: Mixed. Growth is soft: the economy grew an annualised 0.2% in the fourth quarter, below expectations, and it only narrowly avoided a technical recession in 2025. The yen fell after the soft figures, and the IMF urges Japan to keep raising rates and to avoid a sales-tax cut. Political backing is strong: Takaichi's cabinet is at 69% support after the election landslide, which gives the government room to push fiscal reform.

Activity & Currency: USD/JPY is at 153.61, down 2.89% over 20 sessions, a firmer yen over the month (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17). The Nikkei 225 closed at 56,566.49, up 5.57% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17), after the post-election rally in stocks. Exports jumped nearly 17% in January and the finance ministry projects Japan's debt issuance to surge 28% in fiscal 2029 from 2026. The yield curve twist-steepened on fiscal concerns and the BOJ outlook.

Playbook ✓: Mixed. Keep Japanese equity exposure but hedge the yen: the Nikkei's 5.57% gain over 20 sessions rests on export and deal-linked names, while USD/JPY has already fallen 2.89% over the same period. Buy the yen on a BOJ hike path, since an ex-board member expects a rate increase in April and the IMF backs the direction. The call turns Bearish on Japanese equities if the yen weakens again after the soft growth figures, which would mean the hike path is being priced out. Watch the Takaichi budget-reform framework as the signal for bond supply and the curve.

Macro Stance: Mixed. The RBA has tightened and its minutes show a material shift in inflation risks. The bank said a material shift in the economic outlook drove the rate hike and that it sees no set path for future rates. Forecasters think the hike may be a one-off, but the governor has warned the bank will raise rates again if inflation becomes entrenched.

Demand & Financing: AUD/USD is at 0.7073 and up 5.41% over 20 sessions, and the ASX 200 closed at 8,958.90, up 0.95% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17). Wages are the RBA's problem: high wage growth reinforces its inflation challenge, and workers are going backwards as wage growth lags inflation. Bank earnings carry the index: Judo outshone the big banks after a near-50% profit surge, and CBA's profit topped estimates on business loans. Resource-linked demand is fragile: Santos is cutting 10% of jobs and reviewing its portfolio. The RBA's deputy governor says changes to three key facts prompted the rate rise, so the path depends on those facts rather than on a schedule.

Playbook ✓: Mixed. Favour high-quality financials, where earnings are visible, over resources-led cyclicals, where Santos-style cost cuts are spreading. Hedge the Aussie rally (AUD/USD up 5.41% over 20 sessions) if the next wage print reinforces the RBA's inflation worry. The call turns Bullish on the market if the RBA's 'no set path' becomes a pause, and Bearish if the wage-price squeeze pushes the bank to hike again.

Monetary & Activity: Growth is the strong leg. GDP accelerated to 4% in the fourth quarter, and January inflation came in above forecasts. Bankier's headline reads 'inflation surprised, but the MPC will not back off; the decision is already settled', so cuts are off the table for now. Bond yields are below 5%, the lowest in two years, which keeps funding costs contained even as the rate path stays flat.

FX & Markets: USD/PLN is at 3.5548, down 1.96% over 20 sessions, and EUR/PLN at 4.2131 is down 0.22% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17). The Polish equity ETF EPOL is at 37.50, up 4.4% over 20 sessions, and the WIG20 total-return tracker (ETFBW20TR.WA) is at 66.06, up 1.63%. The WIG20 is in a correction, and KGHM's shares are falling with silver. The WIG20 correction is the watch point for the index.

Companies: KGHM signed a €6bn copper agreement with NKT, yet the shares fell as silver weakened; KGH.WA closed at 285.30, down 10.82% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17). PKO Bank Polski plans foreign expansion and cut the rate on its best deposit; PKO.WA at 89.20 is up 2.13% over 20 sessions. Orlen expanded its Norwegian gas portfolio with the Afrodite stake, and PKN.WA at 106.46 is up 9.14%. PGE is building a new gas heat source, and PGE.WA at 10.21 is up 14.93%. PZU.WA at 68.52 is down 1.5%.

Security & New Development: The EU approved €44bn of SAFE defence loans for Poland, with first funds expected in March. Poland's Piorun man-portable air-defence system is drawing interest from Germany, Ukraine and France, and Poland has banned Chinese-made vehicles from military sites over spy-sensor fears. Northrop Grumman and a Polish arms maker plan to produce more than 180,000 artillery shells a year in Poland. The security backdrop is live: Poland closed the Rzeszów and Lublin airports after a Russian missile attack on Ukraine.

Playbook ✓: Mixed. The rates story points to a hold: a 4% GDP print and inflation above forecasts mean cuts are not coming soon, so favour banks and cash-generative exporters over rate-sensitive builders. PKO.WA (up 2.13% over 20 sessions) is the liquid expression, and EPOL (up 4.4%) and the WIG20 tracker (up 1.63%) carry the defence-capex link. The trigger for a bullish call is the first SAFE disbursement in March. The call turns Bearish if the WIG20 correction deepens while the budget gap widens. ⚠ Divergence: growth at 4% and bond yields below 5% point to lower funding costs, yet the year opened with a budget deficit and inflation surprised to the upside, which argues the central bank keeps rates steady.

Narrative: The consensus is that AI spending keeps tech earnings rising, but the market now prices disruption risk for software and services. XLK is down 4.22% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17), and the software selloff has spread: JPMorgan flags 'AI-resilient' software names after the sell-off, while investors are snubbing the dip for deeper AI disruption. Anthropic's Claude Sonnet 4.6 release sent software stocks lower.

Reported: Cadence beat quarterly profit and revenue estimates on strong AI-linked demand. Palo Alto Networks beat by $0.09, but its shares slumped 7% as third-quarter profit guidance fell short, and it cut its annual profit forecast as deal costs bit. Microsoft posted the largest earnings beat in its history, yet investors dumped the shares.

EPS Upside Watch: Nvidia's pending print and its FY26-close preview frame the next leg for the group. Meta's expanded Nvidia pact for millions of chips gives the chain visible demand. The set-up favours semis over software: Nvidia is down 0.68% over 20 sessions while the sector's SOXX is up 3.40%, so the surprise is more likely to come from chip demand than from software revisions.

⚡ Breaking Convention: The consensus says AI capex lifts tech across the board, but Microsoft's record beat sold off and Cisco fell 7% on a mediocre forecast even though earnings topped estimates. The breaking signal is that the beat-and-sell pattern has reached the largest platforms, not only small caps, so the sector's leadership is less secure than the index suggests.

Narrative: Communication services is a capex story. Meta is deepening its Nvidia ties with a pact for millions of chips, and Alphabet is funding the build-out with debt, including a 100-year sterling bond. XLC is down 0.67% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17), which means the market is treating the capex as a cost before it is treated as a return.

Reported: Reddit's shares moved on an insider vote of confidence after its earnings, and the stock has been under pressure, down 46% in a month. Netflix trades at 77.00, down 12.5% over 20 sessions, and analysts see 55% upside on the stock (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17). The feed carries no major results from the largest names in the window.

EPS Upside Watch: Netflix is the cleanest set-up. The stock has de-rated sharply and analysts' target-price work sees 55% upside, so a beat-and-hold quarter would be the most likely upside surprise in the sector. Meta's chip deal is a demand signal rather than an EPS one, and its benefit to the group will show up in capex and depreciation before it shows in revenue.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Reddit's revenue soars while its stock falls and its sentiment crashes, which cuts against the idea that platform revenue growth protects the multiple. The market is pricing the platforms' ad and AI risk, not their growth, so the sector's growth names are not automatically rewarded.

Narrative: The consensus is that banks are the one area where earnings are beating. NatWest's profit rose 24% and beat estimates, and NAB's cash earnings rose 16% to $2bn, a record for the stock. Regulation is easing too: the Fed is set to loosen bank rules to boost mortgage lending. Even so, the US financial ETF XLF is down 4.11% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17).

Reported: NatWest beat estimates with a 24% profit surge, and KBC's fourth-quarter profit narrowly beat consensus. Commerzbank lifted its outlook after a profit beat and a strong January, and CBA's dividend will be A$2.35. The results have been strong across European and Australian banks, and the feed shows the same pattern in each.

EPS Upside Watch: Commerzbank's guidance may be conservative, which makes the next guidance raise the likely surprise in European banks. Australia's ANZ CEO's strategy has investor backing after a solid first-quarter result, so the regional banks with visible strategy delivery are the set-up. Among US names, JPMorgan (307.13, down 1.71% over 20 sessions) and Goldman Sachs (916.04, down 4.78%) carry the same bank-earnings read through their trading and fee lines.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Banks shone on the AI-uncertainty week, yet the sector ETF is still down 4.11% over 20 sessions. The rally in bank stocks is not carrying the index. The cut against the narrative is that deregulation and strong results are not enough to lift the financial ETF while the broader market is de-rating on AI disruption fears.

Narrative: Energy is the sector with the strongest 20-session move: XLE is up 12.71% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17). The driver that matters now is the US-Iran talks. Brent is at 67.42, up 5.13% over 20 sessions, and WTI at 62.33, up 4.86%. Oil slid 2% to a two-week low on talk of progress, and the Venezuela oil revival is adding supply at the margin.

Reported: TotalEnergies cut its buyback and said profit slipped on lower oil prices. Devon Energy reported fourth-quarter and full-year 2025 results and declared its quarterly fixed dividend. The US has allowed oil majors to resume Venezuela operations and waived Venezuela oil sanctions, which matters for the supply side of the sector.

EPS Upside Watch: The set-up favours the producers that already hold a crude premium. Venezuela's reopening is a supply risk to that premium, but the US Treasury's waiver for oil-sector operations is a positive for companies with exposure there. The upside surprise needs Brent to hold above the level it reached in the rally, which is a crude call rather than an earnings one.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Energy stocks are rallying into falling oil. XLE's 12.71% gain over 20 sessions coexists with oil falling on talk of progress. That is the cut against the narrative, and it suggests investors are paying for something other than the crude spot price, such as dividends, buybacks or a supply premium that the talks could erode.

Narrative: The driver is electrification and data-centre power. Siemens raised its 2026 outlook on AI and data-centre demand, and Magna's fourth-quarter restructuring is paying off. XLI is up 4.9% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17), and Caterpillar is up 18.22% over the same period, a move the sector is pricing as an AI-infrastructure beneficiary.

Reported: Siemens shares jumped on a lifted outlook and a market-view beat. Magna's fourth-quarter results were outstanding. GE Aerospace has rallied 51.5% over the past year, and its 20-session move is small at 0.6%, so the year's gain is not a recent re-rating.

EPS Upside Watch: The set-up favours capital-goods names with data-centre exposure. Siemens' AI and data-centre-driven outlook is the template, and the Caterpillar move already reflects the post-Q4 read. The surprise to watch is whether order books convert into a raised guide, which the feed does not yet show for the group.

⚡ Breaking Convention: The consensus is that US capex will flow through to industrial exporters, but Japan's $550 billion capital commitment to the US is stuck in committee. That cuts against the simple read-through, because the largest pledged investment has not moved yet, so the industrial tailwind is less certain than the rally implies.

Narrative: The consumer is K-shaped. General Mills cut its outlook on weak consumer sentiment, and the consumer discretionary ETF XLY is down 5.12% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17). The stress points are housing and offices: January home sales posted their biggest monthly decline in nearly four years, and the office market is as K-shaped as the US economy.

Reported: McDonald's beat global sales estimates as its value bets paid off, and its value campaign is working. Restaurant Brands shares fell despite an earnings beat. Airbnb's shares rose on a revenue beat and rosy guidance, and Deutsche Bank upgraded Airbnb on the beat and AI momentum.

EPS Upside Watch: Nike's CEO sees momentum building with retailers and outdoor gear, which is the one discretionary set-up the feed offers. Value-led chains such as McDonald's have shown that price-led traffic can beat, so the upside is in companies with a clear value proposition. Consumer sentiment remains the downside risk for the rest of the group.

⚡ Breaking Convention: The cut against the bearish narrative is Airbnb: Deutsche Bank's upgrade came on a discretionary name, showing that the sector's leaders can still be re-rated on beats when guidance is strong. The sector's weakness is concentrated in consumer-staples-adjacent and food names rather than all of discretionary spending.

Narrative: Defensive staples have rallied, with XLP up 7.42% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17) as investors rotate away from tech. Walmart is up 7.64% over 20 sessions, but its shares fell 3.76% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17), a sign that the group's gains are being taken on individual days.

Reported: Coca-Cola's fourth-quarter beat drew analyst price-target raises. Hormel agreed to sell its whole-bird turkey business. General Mills cut its sales forecast, and food stocks tumbled on the warning, with the shares of the company reacting to a weak consumer.

EPS Upside Watch: Coca-Cola's beat and the analyst upgrades set up staples for a beat if pricing holds. General Mills' cut is the warning: the EPS risk for the group is volume rather than price, and the next set of results will show whether shoppers keep trading down.

⚡ Breaking Convention: The cut against the defensive narrative is that food names fell on a guidance cut even as the sector ETF rose 7.42% over 20 sessions. Staples are not one trade; the sector's gain is concentrated in larger names with pricing power, while food-category sellers are being punished for volume.

Narrative: Healthcare is a stock-picking market. Eli Lilly is making a $1 billion AI bet on drug discovery, and the sector's biggest managed-care name, UnitedHealth, is down 12.67% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17). XLV is up 1.05% over the same period, so the sector's gain is narrow.

Reported: Medtronic posted better-than-expected earnings, but its unchanged annual outlook clouded the quarter and the stock fell. Moderna beat quarterly revenue estimates on resilient COVID-shot sales, yet its shares slipped after the report. Gilead's 2026 outlook fell short of Wall Street's view.

EPS Upside Watch: Lilly is the most consistent beat story in the feed: it blew past quarterly estimates and posted a strong outlook in early February. The surprise for the group depends on whether guidance rises, and the feed's pattern (Medtronic, Gilead) shows that flat or cautious guidance is punished even when the quarter beats.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Medtronic is the cut against the consensus. A beat with an unchanged annual outlook is punished, which is a reminder that guidance, not the quarter, sets the healthcare multiple. The same logic that lifts Lilly's shares on an outlook raise is the one that takes Medtronic lower.

Narrative: Copper is an AI and grid-capex asset here, not a growth gauge. BHP's copper profits outran iron ore on AI-driven demand, and Antofagasta's profit jumped 52% on record copper prices. XLB is up 8.26% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17), and Freeport-McMoRan (FCX) at 61.09 is up 4.05%.

Reported: BHP beat forecasts as copper topped iron ore in earnings, and Antofagasta's profit rose 52%. Capstone Copper announced its 2026 guidance. The reporting pattern is record prices lifting the producers, with the margin question moving to processing.

EPS Upside Watch: Producers with record prices and a processing advantage are the surprise candidates. Copper displaces iron ore as BHP's best earner, and Antofagasta's margin is the one to watch. The weak link is the smelter: acid, not copper, is paying Chinese smelters, which could turn a price rally into a processing-margin story.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Copper slid as record stockpiles surged and demand worries grew, and the FT says the US copper problem is processing, not supply. The cut against the bullish narrative is that a record-price story runs into inventory and processing constraints, so the sector's gains rest on prices the market is already testing.

Narrative: Real estate is caught between cheaper mortgages and weaker turnover. Mortgage rates fell to new lows and XLRE is up 4.10% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17). But January home sales posted the biggest monthly decline in nearly four years, and Realtor.com says the affordability crisis is driving unprecedented price cuts.

Reported: The sector's report card in the window is the housing data. January sales fell more than 8%, and CMHC reports that housing starts continue to slide. Big Tech buying up land is also squeezing home builders, who cannot compete for it.

EPS Upside Watch: Earnings momentum is thin, so the upside is in volume. Three-percent mortgages are now outnumbered by payments at 6%, a locked-in market that could loosen if rates keep falling. The first sign would be turnover rising after the record-low mortgage quotes; the feed does not yet show that.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Lower mortgage rates are not lifting the sector's volume. Big Tech's land buying and falling sales cut against the idea that cheaper financing is enough. The sector's 4.10% gain is a rate bet on turnover that the housing data has not yet confirmed. The turnover signal to watch is the next monthly sales print.

Narrative: Utilities are the data-centre power trade. AEP's contracted large-load pipeline doubled to 56 GW, Duke has a $103B spending plan, the largest of any regulated US utility, and Exelon's capital plan is $41.3B, driven by transmission. XLU is up 6.89% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17).

Reported: DTE Energy's five-year spending plan jumped 20% on data-centre and reliability investment. PG&E says data-centre growth has cut its rates 11% since 2024, and Entergy sees traditional and high-tech industrials driving sales growth. The reporting wave is capex-led, and the pipeline is the number to track. The spending plans are the best evidence that the demand is contracted rather than speculative.

EPS Upside Watch: AEP and Entergy have the clearest demand signal, and the surprise is in large-load contracts converting to earnings. Vistra's five-session gain of 13.54% shows the market already pricing the power-for-data-centres theme (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17).

⚡ Breaking Convention: The cut against the utility narrative is policy. Navarro says the administration may force data-centre builders to internalise the costs of the build-out. If that happens, the pace of the pipeline that the spending plans depend on becomes a political variable rather than a demand one.

Narrative: European autos are a tariff and margin story. Mercedes was hit by $1.2 billion of tariff costs as full-year earnings more than halved, and it flagged more margin pressure ahead. The European autos ETF (EXV5.DE) is up 4.41% over 20 sessions in euro terms (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17), a value rebound that is ahead of the margin evidence.
Reported: Mercedes' 2025 earnings more than halved on tariff costs and China woes. Nissan's losses deepened in the last quarter. The Magna quarter was the exception, with restructuring paying off.

EPS Upside Watch: The set-up is for a surprise from tariff relief. Chinese EV makers expect to seek EU tariff relief after VW's win on the Cupra Tavascan case, and Volkswagen (VOW3.DE, up 6.77% over 20 sessions) is the company whose shares already reflect that. The EPS upside is in VW's tariff exposure, while Mercedes carries the downside.

⚡ Breaking Convention: The cut against the bearish narrative is VW. Its tariff win suggests the EU is not closing the door on China-built EVs as firmly as the Mercedes margin story implies. The pressure is on margin and China volumes rather than on market access.

Narrative: Semis are the sector to own on AI capex, with rotation inside the group. SOXX is up 3.40% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17) and SMH is up 1.78%.
